title: Dissipation dilution enhances SiV coupling to vdW diamond nanomechanics
authors: Guanhao Huang, Amberly Xie, Chang Jin, Evelyn Hu, Marko Lončar
abstract: Solid-state color centers embedded into mechanical resonators, where orbital states mediate interactions between spins and long-lived phonons, are a promising platform for hybrid quantum systems. The negatively charged silicon vacancy center in diamond (SiV-) is particularly favorable for strain-coupling to nanomechanical resonators because of its large spin-strain susceptibility and compatibility with device integration. Tensioned nanomechanical resonators offer an attractive route due to their ultra-long mechanical coherence times enabled by diluting defect-induced dissipation, though it is unclear if the same dilution effect undermines strain-mediated coupling to material defect centers. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a tensioned diamond nanobeam platform that enables enhanced strain coupling to SiV- orbital states. Through monitoring the optical response of the SiVs to the static and dynamical strain of the mechanical resonator, we observe that dynamical strain localizes near the clamps of these resonators under static strain. This allows us to enhance SiV-mechanical coupling and the mechanical coherence simultaneously, and provide a SiV-strain sensitivity with greatly improved accuracy over previous literature values. Thus, our work opens a pathway towards seconds-long coherence hybrid quantum systems utilizing point defects in diamond nanomechanics for quantum information processing.
summary: This paper reports on an experimental platform using SiV color centers in tensioned diamond nanobeams to create hybrid quantum systems. By engineering the mechanical environment, the researchers simultaneously enhance the coupling between the SiV spins and mechanical vibrations while extending the system's coherence time. This work provides a highly accurate method for strain sensing and opens a pathway for quantum information processing using point defects.
main_problem: Developing hybrid quantum systems that combine strong quantum interactions with long coherence times while overcoming decoherence sources from material defects.
main_result: The authors demonstrated that tensioning the diamond nanobeam enhances SiV-mechanical coupling and mechanical coherence simultaneously, achieving a highly accurate strain sensitivity.
method: They monitored the optical response (PL) of SiV centers to static and dynamical strain applied to a tensioned diamond nanobeam resonator.
model_or_system: The platform uses negatively charged silicon vacancy centers ($	ext{SiV}^-$) embedded in tensioned diamond nanobeams. These centers couple their orbital states to mechanical vibrations (phonons) mediated by strain.
key_observables: SiV optical response (PL spectra), strain susceptibility, orbital-phonon coupling rates ($	ilde{g}_{	ext{orbit}}$), and mechanical coherence times ($Q_m$).
important_parameters: Tension ($\sigma$), mechanical quality factor ($Q_m$), strain enhancement factor, and coupling rates ($	ext{g}_{	ext{spin}} / 2\pi$).
main_assumptions: The method overcomes systematic uncertainties from previous work by using a strain profile uniform across different SiV implantation depths.
figures_summary: Figures show enhanced SiV-mechanical coupling profiles, the localization of dynamical strain near clamps under static stress, and comparisons of measured strain susceptibilities against theory.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the need for high-coherence, strongly coupled quantum platforms. It details the use of tensioned nanobeams to achieve dissipation dilution and strain localization. Key results demonstrate enhanced coupling rates and accurate strain sensing, opening a pathway for quantum information processing.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the physical realization of solid-state qubits coupled to mechanical oscillators, a core topic in quantum transduction and quantum computing architectures.
